requirement:
`ValidationCache::usage()` returns an owned snapshot of the cache’s lifetime
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. A newly constructed
cache starts at zero. Every agent call through the cache or any clone adds its
usage exactly once by the time the call returns, including retries and failed
attempts. Concurrent calls contribute to the same totals. The snapshot sums tool invocations and result bytes by tool name across validators under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name`. Reading a snapshot
preserves the counters, and later calls leave earlier snapshots unchanged.

```rust,ignore
impl<D: Domain> ValidationCache<D> {
    pub fn usage(&self) -> UsageStats;
}
```
rationale:
I judged the tests against each clause of `requirements.sdk.validation-cache.usage`. I read the supplied test bodies and did not request implementation source.

- **Starts at zero.** `agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs` takes `cache.usage()` before any call. It asserts `initial.attempts == 0` and `initial.tools.is_empty()`.
- **Retries and failed attempts.** `cache_retains_usage_across_validators_and_sums_each_token_category` runs a throttled failure and then a retry. It asserts the cache totals: attempts 3, retries 1, failed_attempts 1. It also asserts the per-category token sums and the prepared and delivered input counts.
  - `validators_keep_measured_tokens_after_failed_attempts_and_evidence_reuse` covers a permanent failure, a retry and evidence reuse. It asserts attempts 3, retries 1, failed_attempts 2, and the token counts, for both the validator and the cache.
- **Added once by the time the call returns.** Each test reads `cache.usage()` after the awaited call returns and asserts exact counts, so double counting or missing counts would fail. `dropping_an_inflight_request_preserves_its_attempt` covers a cancelled in-flight request. It asserts that the cache records 1 attempt.
- **Cache and any clone.** `cache_retains_usage_across_validators_and_sums_each_token_category` builds a validator on `graph` and another on its clone `peer`. It asserts that `graph.cache().usage()`, `peer.cache().usage()` and the retained `cache` all show 3 attempts.
- **Concurrent calls share totals.** `agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces` joins two validators concurrently and uses a barrier to force overlap. It asserts `cache.usage().attempts == 6`, which is 3 per validator.
- **Tool sums by name across validators.** The same test asserts that the cache has 3 tool entries. For each of `read_node`, `get_next_page` and `submit_result`, it asserts calls of 1 per validator and 2 in the cache. It asserts `totals[name].result_bytes` equals the sum of the two validators' bytes. It also asserts that bytes are positive for the tools that return content. This covers the cited `ToolUsage.by_name` as applied here.
- **Snapshots are unchanged by later calls, and reads preserve counters.** `initial` is still zero after the later calls. `before_failure` in `validators_keep_measured_tokens_after_failed_attempts_and_evidence_reuse` still shows failed_attempts 1 after a later failure raises the live total to 2. Repeated `cache.usage()` reads in the tests give consistent values.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept, and I found no marking gaps.

text: `ValidationCache::usage()` returns an owned snapshot of the cache’s lifetime
cache starts at zero. Every agent call through the cache or any clone adds its
usage exactly once by the time the call returns, including retries and failed

attempts. Concurrent calls contribute to the same totals. The snapshot sums tool invocations and result bytes by tool name across validators under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name`. Reading a snapshot
preserves the counters, and later calls leave earlier snapshots unchanged.

`UsageStats` exposes the following totals. `attempts` counts each request sent to the provider once. `retries` counts attempts that repeat a failed request. `failed_attempts` counts attempts that returned a provider error, including those followed by a successful retry.

`prepared_inputs` counts inputs prepared for agent messages. Each node inserted in the opening message counts once. Each requested `read_node` page and each `outgoing_edges` result counts once, including repeated reads. A requested search page counts one input per excerpt on that page. Source listings, search finalization, and opaque custom-tool results contribute zero.

`delivered_inputs` counts those inputs when the provider first responds successfully to the request carrying them. Each input counts once across retries and subsequent turns that replay the same conversation history. For example, if the opening message supplies three nodes and the provider fails permanently before replying, usage records three prepared inputs and zero delivered inputs.
`UsageStats::tools` starts empty and holds one entry per invoked tool, keyed by name. This includes built-in and registered tools.
